title: Monday 23 November 2026

credit.entryTitle: Monday 23 November 2026: 33 stories, 7 regions - Nvidia reinstates Huang, NATO talks after missiles hit Poland, Dymer toll rises to 11

kicker: THE WORLD IN ONE DAY · ONE PAGE

tldr.hook: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO; shares rose more than 28.2%.
points: Wall Street indexes jumped, with the Nasdaq up nearly 6% and chip stocks leading gains.
Huang returned after pressure from US President Donald Trump.
The board vote was unanimous; Colette Kress hands back interim duties and stays CFO.

tldr.hook: NATO's top body was to meet Monday after Russian missiles and a drone fell in Poland.
points: Poland says two cruise missiles, likely Kh-101s, and a jet drone crossed into its airspace.
No one was injured and no infrastructure damage was recorded, Poland's defense minister said.
Poland will present options for bolstering defenses at the meeting; no new deployments announced.

stories.summary: Ambassadors of all 32 allies meet. Poland says Russian missiles, one a Kh-101, fell on Friday.

tldr.hook: Death toll from a Russian drone strike on a Dymer apartment block rose to 11.
points: Police said two people were still missing and seven injured, two of them children.
Rescuers found seven-year-old Davyd alive after 14 hours under the debris.
The drone hit the five-storey block early on November 22 and destroyed one section.

stories.summary: Officials say rescuers found another body on Monday. The dead include a teenager.

tldr.hook: The European Commission proposed new Russia sanctions on banks, ships and sport.
points: The plan would remove about 60 Russian banks from SWIFT and extend transaction bans.
It targets more than 70 vessels and would bar Russian-flag teams from European events.
The package still needs approval by EU member governments; Brussels seeks a December deal.

tldr.hook: Zambia's opposition leader Brian Mundubile was indicted on treason charges.
points: He finished second to Hakinde Hichileme in the August general election.
He and his running mate were held two weeks later and charged alongside 12 others.
A magistrate sent the case to the High Court; no trial date is set; conviction carries up to life.

stories.headline: Zambia's opposition chief indicted

tldr.hook: Russia summoned Estonia's envoy and protested border closures, warning of open war.
points: Moscow protested Tallinn's plan to shut three road crossings from December 1.
The crossings are Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula; the closure is set for six months.
Estonia denied allowing Ukraine to use its airspace for drone attacks on Russia.

tldr.hook: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three in Gaza, including UNRWA worker Adel al-Helo.
points: The strike hit near a water well in Jabalia camp that was manned by UNRWA staff and a guard.
Three others were wounded in the strike.
A second strike on a vehicle in western Gaza City killed two people and wounded others.

tldr.hook: India pledged $1.6bn to Nepal as PM Balen Shah visited Delhi
points: Most of the package is a credit line for energy projects; about $400m is grants for reconstruction.
Nepal gained access to Kandla and Paradip ports and a new Ayodhya-Janakpur train service.
Floods killed more than 1,400 people; rebuilding could cost up to $4.8bn.

points: Police revised an earlier toll after rescuers retrieved bodies from the rubble.
Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Serang district caught fire Saturday afternoon, trapping workers.

tldr.hook: Drones hit a Cúcuta police base, injuring at least three civilians including a baby.
points: The attack damaged 60 homes; officials did not say who was responsible.
De la Espriella stepped up offensives; armed groups struck bases with drones and roadside bombs.

tldr.hook: FIFA confirmed US-led bid with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for 2031 Women's World Cup
points: FIFA ratified the UK bid with England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales for 2035.
The 2031 and 2035 editions will be the first with 48 teams and 104 games.
The US-led bid offers 20 cities: 14 in the US, four in Mexico, San José and Kingston.

tldr.hook: New Zealand held on for a draw in the first Test against India in Wellington.
points: New Zealand finished 239-5, with Daryl Mitchell 49 not out and Glenn Phillips 26 not out.
India declared at 720-9, the highest Test score on New Zealand soil; New Zealand made 368.
The second Test starts in Christchurch on Friday.

tldr.hook: Finland summoned Russia's ambassador over a suspected helicopter airspace violation
points: Finland's defense ministry said the helicopter entered its territory by some 4.1 kilometers.
The ministry condemned Russia's strikes on civilian targets in Ukraine.
Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen linked the incursion to operations around the cargo ship Sparta II.

tldr.hook: Belgian air traffic controllers join a national strike, halting commercial flights
points: Skeyes suspended regular air traffic control from 7 am to 9 pm local time (0600-2000 GMT).
Brussels Airport expected 59,500 passengers on 429 flights Monday, including 213 departures.
An airline group said it is the 11th strike affecting Belgian airspace in 11 months.

links.title: National strike to halt commercial flights in Belgium on Monday

tldr.hook: Zelensky called for Ukraine, Russia, US and Europe talks as soon as possible.
points: Zelensky said Kyiv is ready to meet as early as Tuesday.
Zelensky repeated calls for NATO membership and more air defence weapons from allies.
Rutte said not all NATO allies agree on Ukraine joining; Zelensky said guarantee details unclear.

tldr.hook: Denmark's Supreme Court upheld a law that lets housing estates evict non-Western tenants.
points: The Supreme Court rejected seven families' appeal over 91 terminated leases in Helsingor.
The court ruled the law's non-Western criterion neutral, not based on ethnic origin.
Tenants' associations say 11,000 people will be relocated by 2030.

tldr.hook: 450 German schools and Danish schools got identical bomb threats; police saw no danger.
points: About 450 schools were affected in Germany; Danish police called the threats unfounded.
Authorities declined to recommend evacuations, though some schools sent pupils home as a precaution.
A Reuters tally linked more than 8,000 threats since October to emails under a Russian group's name.

Forecasters expect the cold snap in northwestern Europe to last until early December
Norway pipeline disruptions and Middle East LNG supply disruption tightened supply

Senegal led 5-0 at half-time and top Group F on four points, ahead of Croatia on goal difference.

points: At a Justice Department event, Trump directed the attorney general to speed federal death sentences.
Newsom commuted more than 500 California death sentences to life earlier this month.
